subject: Biotechnology
title: Radiation Protection in Space
description: A quick win: understand Radiation Protection in Space.

hook.text: Cosmic rays damage astronaut DNA — biotech solutions from radiation-resistant organisms may protect crews on deep space missions.

buildup.text: Dsup protein from tardigrades shields DNA from radiation — when expressed in human cells, it reduced radiation damage by 40%.

discovery.text: Melanin from fungi absorbs radiation as an energy source — radiotrophic fungi on Chernobyl's reactor walls grow toward radiation.

twist.text: Modifying astronauts genetically for radiation resistance crosses ethical lines — biotech shields beat human enhancement.

climax.text: Melanin-containing biomaterials could line spacecraft walls — a biological radiation shield grown from fungal cultures in space.

punchline.text: Lessons from extremophiles — biotech shields space travelers from cosmic radiation.

quiz.question: How could tardigrade proteins protect astronauts from radiation?
options: They absorb cosmic rays and convert them to energy
The Dsup protein shields DNA from radiation damage and reduced radiation injury by 40% in human cells
They repair DNA damage after radiation exposure has occurred
